contamination_notice: The canonical truth had already been revealed when workflow v2 was implemented. These are regression claims, not blind discoveries or evidence of generalization.
configuration: Node 24, solc-js 0.8.30 optimizer 200/EVM Paris, Ganache 7.9.2 Shanghai/chain 31337, unmodified target contracts

candidates.title: Two attacker-controlled valuation rates close a flash-funded market drain
candidates.root_cause: The market multiplies an instantaneous pool spot price by a vault exchange rate that direct transfers can change, without independent valuation, smoothing, or manipulation resistance.
candidates.attacker_path: Post 1,000 vault shares, flash-borrow 100,000 stable, swap it through the shallow pool, donate 8,000 received assets to the vault, borrow 150,000, and repay 100,050 to the lender in the same transaction.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: Spot manipulation alone leaves the limit below flash repayment; the joined rates raise it above 150,000. The lender is repaid, the actor retains 49,950 stable, and the market loses 150,000 to undercollateralized debt.
candidates.negative_control: With a durable positive primary feed, the identical funded join reverts and leaves zero debt and zero attacker stable.

candidates.title: Fallback oracle trusts an instantaneous constant-product reserve ratio
candidates.root_cause: A nonpositive feed answer selects the pool's current reserve ratio without a TWAP, delay, or manipulation check, and lending consumes it directly.
candidates.attacker_path: Swap stable into the permissionless shallow pool in the same block, then use the resulting fallback price in the collateral health calculation.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: The retained packet moves the oracle above 100 stable per asset and borrows materially more than the one-dollar comparator permits.
candidates.negative_control: The safe-price comparator limits debt to contemporaneous collateral value.

candidates.title: Unsolicited vault balances inflate already-posted lending collateral
candidates.root_cause: The vault treats its full token balance as managed assets and the market accepts the resulting instantaneous share rate as collateral value.
candidates.attacker_path: After a borrower posts fixed vault shares, an attacker transfers underlying directly to the vault without minting new shares.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: The existing borrower's limit rises from 75 to about 143.18 without any collateral-share change.
candidates.negative_control: Transferring the same assets to an address outside the vault leaves the borrow limit unchanged.

candidates.title: Borrow callback withdraws collateral before debt is committed
candidates.root_cause: Borrow transfers value and calls an attacker-controlled receiver before incrementing debt; the sibling withdrawal path observes the stale zero-debt state.
candidates.attacker_path: Post 1,000 shares and call borrow with callback data; onBorrow reenters withdrawCollateral for all posted shares.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: The actor ends with 500 stable and all 1,000 original shares while the market records 500 debt and zero local collateral.
candidates.negative_control: Omitting callback data leaves all posted collateral escrowed after the same borrow.

candidates.title: Collateral-factor authorization permits public increases
candidates.root_cause: The guardian condition reverts non-guardians only when the next factor is less than or equal to the current factor, unintentionally allowing public increases.
candidates.attacker_path: An ordinary account sets the factor from 7,500 to 9,500 bps and borrows against the enlarged limit.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: A non-guardian globally weakens collateralization and increases available debt from the original 750-unit boundary.
candidates.negative_control: A corrected unconditional guardian check rejects the same caller and preserves the factor.

candidates.title: Withdrawal floor rounding can transfer assets while burning zero shares
candidates.root_cause: withdraw reuses floor-rounded convertToShares even though an exact-asset exit must round the required shares upward.
candidates.attacker_path: Create a 2:1 assets-per-share rate with a zero-decimal token, then withdraw one unit from an account holding no shares.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: The caller receives one asset while its share balance and total supply remain unchanged.
candidates.negative_control: At a 1:1 exchange rate the zero-share caller cannot withdraw one unit.

candidates.title: Vault deposit mints claims from requested rather than received assets
candidates.root_cause: Shares are calculated from the nominal assets argument before transfer and the vault never measures its actual balance increase.
candidates.attacker_path: Against an existing holder, a fee-recipient depositor sends a nominal 100 through an ABI-compatible 10% fee token and redeems the excess minted shares.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: The attacker balance rises from 200 to 209 while the incumbent's redeemable value falls from 900 to 891.
candidates.negative_control: With an exact-delta standard token, the cycle preserves both the attacker starting balance and incumbent value.

candidates.title: Transfer authorization omits chain and verifying-contract domain
candidates.root_cause: The signed payload binds neither block.chainid nor the router address, while nonce state is local to each deployment.
candidates.attacker_path: Submit identical signature bytes to two approved router instances on the same chain.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: Twice the signed token amount leaves the owner through two independent nonce namespaces.
candidates.negative_control: A domain-bound comparator rejects the signature at the second router.

candidates.title: Transfer authorization does not bind the recipient
candidates.root_cause: recipient is accepted as calldata but omitted from the signed payload.
candidates.attacker_path: A relayer supplies its own address while executing an otherwise valid owner authorization.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: The relayer receives the full signed amount and consumes the owner's nonce.

candidates.title: Bridge finalization ignores the authenticated remote sender
candidates.root_cause: The gateway reads xDomainMessageSender only for an event and never compares it with the configured remote gateway for the source chain.
candidates.attacker_path: A different remote application originates an honestly relayed message from a configured chain, credits arbitrary shares, and borrows using only that synthetic collateral.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: A mismatching remote creates 1,000 bridge-collateral units and extracts 750 stable without locked backing.
candidates.negative_control: A sender-binding comparator rejects the wrong application and accepts only the configured remote.

candidates.title: Bridge replay state collides across configured source chains
candidates.root_cause: processedNonce is keyed only by nonce rather than by source-chain domain and nonce.
candidates.attacker_path: Relay a legitimate nonce-7 message on one configured chain before a legitimate nonce-7 message on another.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: The first credit succeeds and the second valid cross-chain credit is denied, leaving its beneficiary uncredited.
candidates.negative_control: A chain-and-nonce-keyed comparator accepts both legitimate messages.

candidates.title: Strategy initialization can be repeated to seize privileged roles
candidates.root_cause: initialize is public and never checks or consumes the initialized flag before overwriting vault and operator.
candidates.attacker_path: After legitimate setup and funding, an ordinary account reinitializes both roles, sweeps held tokens, and gains arbitrary-call authority.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: The attacker drains the module balance and seizes its two privileged execution identities.
candidates.negative_control: A one-time initializer comparator rejects the second call.

candidates.title: Primary oracle accepts expired price rounds
candidates.root_cause: price discards round timestamps and completion metadata and accepts any positive answer indefinitely.
candidates.attacker_path: Use an expired positive two-dollar round as the lending valuation input.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: The stale round permits 1,500 stable debt where the current one-dollar value supports 750.
candidates.negative_control: A freshness-checking comparator rejects the same expired round.

candidates.title: Nominal repayment clears more debt than the market receives
candidates.root_cause: repay reduces debt by the requested paid amount without measuring the market's actual stable balance increase.
candidates.attacker_path: Borrow 50 fee-bearing stable and nominally repay 50 through an ABI-compatible token charging 10% on transferFrom.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: Debt becomes zero even though the market receives only 45 and ends five stable below its pre-borrow reserve.
candidates.negative_control: An exact-delta standard token restores the market reserve completely when debt reaches zero.

candidates.title: Raw signature-byte replay protection is bypassed by ECDSA malleability
candidates.root_cause: The distributor keys replay state by signature bytes while recovery accepts equivalent high-s and low-s encodings for the same payload.
candidates.attacker_path: Transform a valid signature to its high-s counterpart and submit both encodings for one reward payload.
candidates.demonstrated_impact: One authorization pays the account twice.
candidates.negative_control: A payload-keyed comparator rejects the alternate encoding.
